topic: Order tasks with dependencies using a topological sort
title: Topological Sort with Kahn's Algorithm

scenes.narration: Each arrow means one task must come before another: A before B and C, and both B and C before D. Kahn's algorithm keeps the tasks whose arrows into them are all gone as ready, and takes the alphabetically first one each step.
scenes.caption: Do every task after what it depends on

scenes.narration: Only A has no incoming arrows, so A is taken first. Removing its arrows frees both B and C, which become ready.
scenes.caption: take A

scenes.narration: B and C are ready, and B comes first alphabetically. Removing the arrow from B leaves D with just one incoming arrow.
scenes.caption: take B

scenes.narration: C is taken next. Its arrow to D was the last one, so D becomes ready.
scenes.caption: take C

scenes.narration: Finally D is taken. The order A, B, C, D respects every arrow.
scenes.caption: take D

scenes.narration: A topological order only exists for graphs without cycles. Build tools, course plans and spreadsheet formulas all rely on it.
scenes.caption: Summary
points: Ready: tasks with no remaining incoming arrows
Take one, remove its arrows, repeat
If nothing is ready but tasks remain, there is a cycle

quiz.question: Arrows: A to C, B to C, C to D, B to E. After taking two tasks, which tasks are ready?
quiz.explanation: Taking A and B removes every arrow into C and E.

quiz.question: Arrows: B to A and C to A. Before any step, which tasks are ready?
quiz.explanation: B and C have no incoming arrows; A waits for both.
